temas.titulo: Unit 1 · Addition, subtraction, multiplication and division
resumen: Being able to calculate **without a calculator** is an important skill. Always check your answer with an **estimate**.
## Mental methods
- **Number bonds** to 10 or 100: 52 + 68 → the units 2 and 8 make 10, so 50 + 60 + 10 = **120**.
- **Same units**: 146 − 36 → 6 − 6 = 0, so it is the same as 140 − 30 = **110**.
- **Borrowed numbers (rounding)**: 79 + 32 → 80 + 32 = 112, then take away the 1 you added: **111**.
- 118 − 44 → 120 − 44 = 76, then take away the 2 you added: **74**.
## Subtracting negative numbers
Subtracting a negative number is the same as **adding** it: 10 − (−3) = 10 + 3 = **13**.
So subtracting a negative number makes the answer **bigger**.
## Estimating
Round each number to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000 to make the calculation easier.
- An estimate helps you spot wrong answers: 1121 + 788 − 210 − (−592) ≈ 1000 + 800 − 200 + 600 = 2200, so an answer of 1291 must be wrong.
## Multiplication and division with negative numbers
- A **negative × positive** gives a **negative** answer: (−3) × 4 = −12
- A **negative ÷ positive** gives a **negative** answer: −12 ÷ 4 = −3
## Using a fact you know

resumen: ## Polygons
A **polygon** is any closed 2D shape made of straight lines. Triangles and quadrilaterals are polygons.
A **regular polygon** has all sides the same length and all interior angles equal (e.g. a square, an equilateral triangle).
- 5 sides: **pentagon** · 6 sides: **hexagon** · 8 sides: **octagon**
## Quadrilaterals
- **Square**: all sides equal, all angles 90°, both pairs of opposite sides parallel, diagonals equal and cross at right angles.
- **Rectangle**: opposite sides equal, all angles 90°, diagonals equal (but they do **not** cross at right angles).
- **Parallelogram**: opposite sides equal and parallel; no right angles; diagonals not equal.
- **Rhombus**: all four sides equal, opposite sides parallel, diagonals cross at right angles.
- **Kite**: two pairs of equal adjacent sides, **no** parallel sides, diagonals cross at right angles.
- **Trapezium**: only **one** pair of parallel sides.
## Congruent shapes
**Congruent** shapes are identical: corresponding sides and angles are equal.
- Two congruent isosceles right-angled triangles can make a **square**, a **parallelogram** or a bigger triangle.
- Two congruent equilateral triangles make a **rhombus**.
## Symmetry
A regular polygon with *n* sides has **n lines of symmetry** and **rotational symmetry of order n**. An equilateral triangle has 3 lines of symmetry and rotational symmetry of order 3.
## Parts of a circle
- **Centre**; **circumference** (the perimeter of a circle).
- **Radius** (plural **radii**): centre to circumference. **Diameter**: a chord through the centre = 2 × radius.
- **Chord**: a straight line joining two points on the circumference.
- **Arc**: part of the circumference.
- **Sector**: area between two radii and an arc. **Segment**: area between an arc and a chord.
- **Tangent**: a straight line that touches the circle at one point. The angle between a radius and a tangent is **90°**.

resumen: ## Types of data
- **Quantitative data** can be measured with numbers. It is either discrete or continuous.
- **Discrete data** can only take specific values, e.g. the number of students in a class (30 is possible, 30.2 is not).
- **Continuous data** can take any value in a range, e.g. time, mass, height, temperature. It is only as accurate as the measurement: 10.228 s is to three **decimal places**.
- **Categorical data** is put into groups (categories), e.g. hair colour, type of transport, football team.
## Population and samples
- The **population** is everybody the survey is about (e.g. everyone in your school), not the whole country.
- Asking everyone can be too time-consuming or expensive, so we ask a **sample**.
- The **sample size** is the number of people asked.
- A sample should be **representative**: its results should be similar to the results of the whole population.
- Ways to choose: every 10th person on a list, or a **random number generator** (fair: everyone has the same chance).
- A sample is not representative if it only includes one group (e.g. one class out of a whole school) or if the sample is too small (20 out of 1500).
- If groups have different sizes, take the sample **in proportion** to their sizes.
## Interviews and questionnaires

**Interview** – advantages: detailed answers, the interviewer can clarify misunderstandings, higher response rate. Disadvantages: needs a skilled interviewer, time-consuming and expensive, smaller sample size.

**Questionnaire** – advantages: can reach a lot of people, cheap, quick, easy to analyse, good for sensitive topics. Disadvantages: not suitable for complex questions, impersonal, some people don't return it, questions may be misunderstood or ignored, answers may be biased.
Good questions are clear, ask one thing at a time and have answer boxes that are easy to analyse.

resumen: ## The formula
A triangle is **half of a rectangle** drawn around it, so:
**Area of a triangle = ½ × base length × perpendicular height**
- The **perpendicular height** is measured at **right angles** to the base.
- Any side can be the base, as long as the height is measured at right angles to it.
- You don't need the sloping sides: a triangle with base 8 cm, height 3 cm and a side of 4 cm has area ½ × 8 × 3 = **12 cm²**.
- Area is measured in square units, e.g. **cm²**.
## Working backwards
If you know the area, you can find a missing length: base = 2 × area ÷ height.
Example: area 100 cm² and base 20 cm → height = 200 ÷ 20 = **10 cm**.
## Triangles with the same base and height
Triangles on the same base between two parallel lines all have the same height, so they all have the **same area**.
## Compound shapes
A **compound shape** is made from two or more simpler shapes. Split it up, find each area and add them.
Example: a rectangle 8 cm × 3 cm plus a triangle with base 3 cm and height 12 − 8 = 4 cm → 24 + 6 = **30 cm²**.

resumen: When a calculation has more than one operation, you must do them in the right order:
- **B**rackets first
- **I**ndices (powers) next, e.g. 8² = 64
- **D**ivision and **M**ultiplication
- **A**ddition and **S**ubtraction last
This is often remembered as **BIDMAS**.
## Worked examples
- 3 × 2² = 3 × 4 = **12** (not 36: the power is done before multiplying)
## Brackets change the answer
- Brackets are sometimes not needed: in 8 + (2 × 6) the multiplication would be done first anyway.
